svg.title: Dictation Operative — DO in 60 seconds
svg.desc: A quick guide to Capture, Refine, and Use, with Mac dictation and device Sync instructions.

g.text: DICTATION OPERATIVE
START HERE · QUICK GUIDE
DO in 60 seconds
From a passing thought to words you can use.
Capture
Refine
Use
Capture
Get the thought down.
In Capture, tap the microphone, speak, then stop. Your transcript saves automatically.
Prefer the keyboard? Choose Write instead or Paste.
Reply to something: paste the message first, then speak your reply points.
Refine
Shape your words.
Open a saved thought. Choose Shape your words to Clean up, Rewrite, or Turn into an AI
prompt. Review the result and save any edits.
Use Add more to this thought to keep going. Your original and saved versions stay available.
Use
Put your words to work.
Copy or share your finished text. Find saved thoughts in Clipboard, pin text you reuse,
or select at least two thoughts in Compose to build a new draft.
In Compose, arrange your thoughts, choose Email, Progress update, or Checklist, then Create
draft.
Try it: three thoughts, one email.
1. Record three project updates.
2. Select and order them in Compose.
3. Choose Email → Create draft.
4. Review, copy, and send in your email app.
On your Mac
Click where you want to type. Tap Control +
Option, speak, then tap again to insert. Or
hold the shortcut while talking and release to
insert.
Set up the native Mac app, microphone and
Accessibility permissions, and a speech model first.
Use your own shortcut if you changed it.
Across devices
Open Sync devices in the workspace and Settings
→ Sync on Mac. Create a pairing code, enter it
on the other device, compare the confirmation
codes, and approve.
Send clipboard or Receive latest transfers text and
images. Keep the web app open and both devices
online. Mac and web histories stay separate.
Allow microphone access and follow voice & AI setup prompts before recording.
Web transcription and AI need internet. Full guide: dictationoperative.com/help
